commit_message:
swscale/output: fix bilinear yuv2rgb chroma interpolation

These functions were divided into two special cases; one assuming that
uvalpha == 0, and the other assuming that uvalpha == 2048. This worked fine
for simple 2x chroma upscaling but broke for e.g. yuv410p, non-centered chroma,
or other special cases that involved non-aligned chroma filters.

Fix it by instead dividing this check into two cases, a uvalpha==0 fast path
and a uvalpha>0 general path. Instead of (A+B)/2 the general path now multiplies
in the true uvalpha weight.

I tried preserving the old fast path for the case of uvalpha == 2048, but this
was significantly slower in practise versus having just one general path.
However, we still need a uvalpha == 0 path for the unscaled case.

Fixes: ticket #5083
Signed-off-by: Niklas Haas <git@haasn.dev>
Sponsored-by: Sovereign Tech Fund

fix_commit.message: swscale/output: fix integer overflow in yuv2rgba64_full_1_c_template()
fix_commit.author: Michael Niedermayer

findings.title: Signed integer overflow computing chroma weighted sum in yuv2rgba64_full_1_c_template()
findings.message: In the uvalpha>0 (bilinear chroma interpolation) branch of yuv2rgba64_full_1_c_template(), the U and V chroma values are computed as a weighted sum of two 32-bit chroma samples multiplied by interpolation weights, then a bias is subtracted, and the result is shifted right: `int U = (ubuf0[i] * uvalpha1 + ubuf1[i] * uvalpha - (128 << 23)) >> 14;` (and analogous line for V). U and V are declared as plain signed `int`. Because ubuf0[i]/ubuf1[i] can be large 32-bit intermediate chroma values and uvalpha/uvalpha1 sum to 4096, the multiply-add can exceed INT_MAX/underflow INT_MIN, producing signed integer overflow, which is undefined behavior in C and was flagged by UBSan/OSS-Fuzz (`signed integer overflow: -293650 * 16525 cannot be represented in type 'int'`). This same pattern was introduced in this commit for both the 64-bit full (yuv2rgba64_full_1_c_template) and non-full (yuv2rgba64_1_c_template) variants when the code was changed from a simple average of two chroma samples to a true weighted multiply based on uvalpha.
findings.suggestion: Declare U and V using the project's SUINT macro (which resolves to `unsigned int` in normal builds and `int` only under the CHECKED/UBSan debug configuration) instead of a bare `int`, so that the arithmetic wraps deterministically under modular unsigned arithmetic rather than invoking signed-overflow undefined behavior. This matches the pattern already used for Y in the same function and was the actual fix applied upstream.
findings.suggestion_code:
SUINT U = (ubuf0[i] * uvalpha1 + ubuf1[i] * uvalpha - (128 << 23)) >> 14;
SUINT V = (vbuf0[i] * uvalpha1 + vbuf1[i] * uvalpha - (128 << 23)) >> 14;

ground_truth.root_cause: When the bilinear chroma interpolation code path was rewritten to use a true weighted average (`ubuf0[i]*uvalpha1 + ubuf1[i]*uvalpha`) instead of the previous simple sum/average (`ubuf0[i] + ubuf1[i]`), the resulting intermediate value's magnitude range increased, but the variable holding it was left declared as a plain signed `int` instead of the project's overflow-tolerant `SUINT` (unsigned int) type that other intermediate values (like Y) in the same function already use to safely allow wraparound instead of hitting signed-overflow UB.
